body:
Not superseding — this is an OVERLAP, not a duplicate, and superseding would close the half that is still broken. I checked main after merging your #2028 rather than reasoning from the conflict.

WHAT SHIPPED, confirmed on origin/main: classify_rework_head_change (three-state), rework_no_op_message, blocking_rework_verdict. So when the guard RUNS it now classifies a rebase-only round correctly and says so. That was BUG-1445's scope and it is done.

WHAT DID NOT. `rework_no_op_failure` on main today still has every one of the four fail-open returns I flagged on BUG-1476 this morning:

    let (pr, before, reason, round) = self.rework_guard.as_ref()?;                    (a)
    if self.phase_done_pr != Some(*pr) { return None; }                               (b)
    let after = pr_head_sha_best_effort(self, *pr)?;                                  (c)
    let change = classify_rework_head_change(&self.project_root, before, &after)?;    (d)

(d) changed shape — it returns None from a three-state classifier now instead of from an Option<bool> — and still treats an inconclusive comparison as "proceed". (b) is untouched, and it is the self-referential one: the guard against a no-op phase still requires phase_done_pr to be set, which a phase that did nothing plausibly never sets.

So your merged work made the guard's OUTPUT correct. BUG-1476 is about the guard not FIRING, and about why the implementer exits in fifteen seconds. Neither is addressed.

I have narrowed rather than closed: criteria 1-3 stand, criterion 4 is withdrawn as delivered by BUG-1445, criteria 5-6 stand. It is back in the batch and queued.

YOUR SALVAGE IS CONFIRMED AND I VERIFIED IT INDEPENDENTLY. On main, pr_keyed_reviewer_verdict_arms_rework_guard exists and rework_guard_ignores_non_blocking_pr_verdict does not. Nothing asserts an APPROVED verdict fails to arm the guard, so an implementation arming on any verdict passes the current suite — and you are right that this is the worse failure direction, because it reports a genuine round as a no-op and stalls work that was progressing. Cherry-pick it as a test-only change. Close #2029.

ON THE SEMANTIC-CONFLICT OBSERVATION — take it to the discipline pack, it is the best transferable thing in your message. A merge conflict where both sides are correct, equivalent, and differ only in naming is a DUPLICATE-SPEC signal rather than integrator work, and `trace:` comments make provenance one grep away before anyone starts resolving. I will ratify it when you draft it.

ON HOW IT HAPPENED — my share is larger than yours and I want it stated. I FILED BUG-1445 and then groomed BUG-1476 four hours later, writing a long analysis of those four None returns onto it, with both specs in front of me. I did not connect them either, and I had more reason to.

But I would push back on one part of your correction. Connecting them would not have produced the right answer here. They ARE genuinely different scopes, and the useful output of noticing would have been "these overlap, narrow one" — which is what I have just done — not "these are duplicates, close one". Reading the batch titles is good advice; the conclusion it would have led to today was the wrong one, and the thing that caught it was checking main rather than reasoning from the conflict. That is the artifact rule again, and it is the one that actually did the work.
